dedupe_keys.name: harmonised global datasets of wind and solar farm locations and power from openstreetmap 2020

description: This dataset gives what its authors describe as the first global, open-access, harmonised spatial datasets of wind and solar photovoltaic installations, built from OpenStreetMap. It was published in Scientific Data in 2020 by Sebastian Dunnett, A. Sorichetta, G. Taylor and co-authors, who note that most studies had used land suitability as a proxy for where infrastructure actually is. It contains global wind turbines as of April 2020 clustered with an 800 m neighbourhood distance and solar PV farms, as point and polygon features for grouped installations with first-order estimates of power capacity, landscape area and panel area; the paper reports that the wind power model captured nearly all variability in turbine numbers in the larger OSM set. Files come in WGS 1984 and Eckert IV projections as shapefile, GeoPackage and CSV in a single zip of about 235 MB, available for free download from figshare under CC0, with code to rebuild newer versions; the figshare record, version 6, was modified in September 2025. Coverage is global. Caveats: completeness follows OSM mapping effort, which is uneven between countries, and capacities are modelled. Simulation uses are locations and capacities of wind and solar farms for exposure analysis and siting studies. Related records: data-global-renewables-watch-solar-wind gives a satellite-derived alternative.
